key_insight: Tuning inter-nanoparticle repulsion produces four morphologies—droplet, slab, crystalline droplet, and dispersed—with distinct effects on polymer ordering.
engineering_relevance: Interparticle repulsion offers a potential design lever for controlling nanoparticle dispersion and polymer organization in confined polymer nanocomposites.
method: Langevin dynamics simulations of nanoparticles in a semiflexible, rod-like polymer matrix under extreme confinement.
Varied nanoparticle–nanoparticle repulsion while holding other interactions fixed.
Analyzed nanoparticle clustering, local crystallinity, and polymer nematic order.
evidence_signal: The slab regime showed the strongest polymer nematic order despite negligible nanoparticle crystallization, while crystalline droplets reduced nematic order and dispersed nanoparticles enabled local smectic-like ordering.
watch_item: Results concern an extremely confined simulation model; transferability to bulk materials or experimental systems remains to be established.
paper_title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
